budgets.reason: no `baseline` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The oracle's own tail, recorded at 105-153 ms across m17: a host artifact big enough to move the far less load-sensitive `sys` side shows up here too, so it cannot be misread as a Rust regression — and 400 ms is deliberately loose because this row exists to attribute, not to gate.

The request-tail budget on the I/O-bound target, recorded at 3.03-3.59 ms p99 while serving ~198k req/s through a real Cowboy release: 5 ms leaves room for a loaded host yet still flags a real latency regression; it reads the summary the cowboy row actually records (`latency_ms` — there is no separate p99 metric) and it is sys-only because the Rust runtime cannot boot an OTP release.
